newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: HK legislator attacks inaction over China abuses.
newsitem.headline: HK legislator attacks inaction over China abuses.

text.p: Hong Kong legislator Martin Lee on Wednesday criticised the West's failure to condemn Chinese human rights abuses and accused Beijing of planning a repressive rule in the territory after Britain hands it over.
"The world is looking starry-eyed to China as a huge future market," Lee told a meeting on China on the fringes of the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva.
"We know that big business people all over the world are telling their governments to keep quiet to Chinese leaders on sensitive matters so as not to lose their trade with China," Lee said.
"If you sit back and do nothing, your silence will encourage China to break a lot of international agreements in the future."

Denmark decided to table a resolution on China at Geneva's U.N. Human Rights forum after France last month opted for dialogue with Beijing rather than confrontation and refused to support a draft European Union motion.
Lee said Beijing was preparing to install authoritarian rule in Hong Kong, which reverts to communist-ruled China on June 30 after 150 years as a British colony.

Lee said China was preparing to muzzle Hong Kong's free press, control its courts and education policy with plans to replace the elected legislature with an appointed body and to water down liberal laws guarding civil liberties and democracy.
"Perhaps I should remind you of the German republic...after Hitler took over. Hitler had the laws changed overnight. Judges who refused were executed," Lee said.
"China has adopted a total hands-on policy on Hong Kong, contrary to its earlier promises. It has already set up all the necessary institutions to exercise this control."
